STEP 1 - Scene: A small side dish or snack-style plate: a mix of fresh berries (blackberries and raspberries) and pickled or cooked vegetables (looks like pale green pickled cucumber/leek-type pieces and a sliced pale vegetable such as cooked leek or chayote).

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 22 cm across. Area ≈ 22 x 22 ≈ 480 cm² (the food sits in the central portion). Food covers only a small part of it.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Blackberries (about 5 berries)
- Raspberries (about 6 small berries/clusters)
- Pickled/cooked green vegetable pieces (cucumber or leek-like slices, about 4-5 pieces)

STEP 4 - Area (percent of plate area, ~480 cm²):
- Blackberries: ~7% (about 34 cm²)
- Raspberries: ~6% (about 29 cm²)
- Green vegetable pieces: ~10% (about 48 cm²)
Total food coverage ≈ 23%.

STEP 5 - Volume (area x height):
- Blackberries: 34 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 51 ml
- Raspberries: 29 cm² x 1.2 cm ≈ 35 ml
- Vegetables: 48 cm² x 1.5 cm ≈ 72 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Blackberries: 51 ml x 0.6 ≈ 31 g
- Raspberries: 35 ml x 0.6 ≈ 21 g
- Vegetables (cut, pickled/cooked): 72 ml x 0.6 ≈ 43 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Blackberries: 31 g x 43 kcal/100g ≈ 13 kcal
- Raspberries: 21 g x 52 kcal/100g ≈ 11 kcal
- Vegetables: 43 g x 20 kcal/100g ≈ 9 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 95 g and ≈ 33 kcal. This is plausible for a small handful of berries and a few vegetable pieces on a large plate, and it is far below a full dinner plate, which matches the sparse coverage.

Total: about 95 g, about 33 kcal.
